caption:
She told me she felt bad that she had to cut through my stomach. 

I was lying in a hospital bed, barely awake, completely out of it when the doctor came in. She said I needed emergency surgery. I nodded, but everything was foggy.

She mentioned there’d be a scar and that she felt bad about it. I didn’t really process it at the time, but somewhere in the back of my mind I wondered: Will that bother me?

It never has.

People ask me if it does, and the truth is… I forget it’s even there. I still wear crop tops. I don’t try to hide it. I’d love to say it’s because I’m proud of it and maybe that’s true… but mostly, I just never let it define me.

That moment wasn’t the end of anything. It was the beginning of my comeback. And my comeback became a part of who I am.

The scar? That’s just a reminder that I’m stronger than the setback.

#comeback #fitness #fitnesslife

caption:
They say, “Don’t spoil your kids.”
I say, “Spoil them rotten.”

But spoil them with time and experiences.

Let me be clear- There is nothing wrong with gifting objects for Christmas! But you’re not failing as a parent if you choose less material possessions and more togetherness.

Because childhood isn’t built on what we give them.
It’s not found in boxes.
It’s built in moments we share with them.

The long walks.
New places.
Learning they can do challenging things.
Problem solving in real world scenarios.
The feeling of being safe, seen, and together, no matter where you are.

This is the kind of childhood we’re choosing for our kids.
Rooted in connection.
Brimming with wonder and magic.
Rich in moments that don’t instantly vaporize.

It’s not perfect.
But it’s wholly present.

And the best part is, you don’t have to travel the world to make it happen.

Find the little adventures nearby.
Do something new and novel.
And then, take it all in. 
Slow down enough for them to root into the experiences;
The walks, the food, the scenery, the challenges, the people, and the feelings. 
That’s what they remember.

The adventures is what makes the magic.
Not the possessions.❤️

➡️ “Can you cite a randomized controlled trial?”
➡️ “Is there meta-analytic evidence?”

No citation.
No trial.
No meta-analysis.
Instead, we get word salad, deflection, and confusion about why randomized controlled trials matter in the first place.
RCTs aren’t a “nice to have.”
They’re the minimum bar when you’re making clinical claims, especially claims tied to diagnostics, treatments, or interventions that people pay for.
If someone says:

Credit where it’s due: Dr. Mike stays calm, presses respectfully, and exposes the gap without grandstanding. This is exactly how pseudoscience gets challenged — not by yelling, but by asking for receipts.
Extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence
End of story.

caption:
“Inflammation” is the biggest buzzword in nutrition

And 99% of the people talking about it have absolutely no clue what it is or how it works

It’s like fitness influencers discovered the word “inflammation” and now suddenly it explains literally everything. Can inflammation affect health markers? Of course. But this idea that inflammation is somehow “locking your fat cells shut” is complete nonsense. There’s no evidence your body is refusing to burn fat because your fat cells are in “survival mode.” People with insulin resistance and high inflammation lose the same amount of body fat under similar calorie deficits as non-insulin resistant, low inflammatory people (PMID: 17023708)

In fact, the research largely shows the opposite direction of causality:
More adipose tissue → more inflammation
Less adipose tissue → less inflammation
Meaning excess body fat itself is a major DRIVER of chronic low-grade inflammation (PMID: 41598484). This guy has the cart completely before the horse.

And then, like clockwork here come all the buzzwords:
✅ inflammation!
✅ cortisol!
✅ insulin resistance!
✅ hormones!

Just a giant buzzword soup designed to scare you into buying an “anti-inflammatory protocol.”
Here’s the reality:
You do NOT need a detox.
You do NOT need a cortisol reset.
You do NOT need a supplement stack blessed by an infrared sauna shaman.

A legitimately anti-inflammatory lifestyle is actually pretty boring:
✅ maintain a healthy body fat level
✅ resistance train regularly
✅ eat enough protein
✅ eat enough fiber
✅ get fruits & vegetables
✅ sleep enough
✅ exercise consistently

Ya know… the boring stuff that WORKS

Ironically, the people selling “anti-inflammatory protocols” usually make nutrition MORE stressful and restrictive, which is probably worse for adherence than the inflammation they’re fearmongering about. Your body composition is mostly governed by energy balance, diet quality, activity, sleep, and consistency over time, not because your fat cells are holding a hostage negotiation with your inflammation and cortisol levels

caption:
LDL cholesterol is one of the most well-established causal risk factors in all of medicine.

And this graph is exactly why.

In my latest podcast episode on seed oils I explain why LDL matters. Anti-seed oil psychos will try to convince you LDL doesn’ matter but the DATA IS CLEAR

Different genetic variants. Different mechanisms. Same result:
Lower lifetime LDL exposure = lower cardiovascular disease risk (PMID: 23083789).

Not kinda.
Not “maybe.”
Not “only if inflammation is high.”
Not “only if LDL is oxidized.”
Not “only if your triglycerides are high.”

The relationship is log-linear and remarkably consistent. That means regardless of HOW LDL is lowered, reducing exposure reduces risk by the SAME amount (~50-55% reduction in CVD risk per 1mmol lifetime reduction in LDL). Statins, PCSK9 inhibitors, ezetimibe, genetics… same pattern.

If you still think LDL cholesterol has nothing to do with cardiovascular disease after looking at this data, then honestly, there’s probably no amount of evidence that will convince you. This is what causality looks like in human data.
And no, saying “but cholesterol is important for hormones/cell membranes/brain function” is not an argument against this. Oxygen is essential for life too, but too much of the wrong thing in the wrong place can still kill you and your body can make plenty of the cholesterol you need with VERY LITTLE cholesterol intake

 - 12 dates
 - 1 cup almonds
 - 1/4 tsp sea salt

3. Spread the creamy pistachio butter over the nougat, then sprinkle with:
 - 1/2 cup chopped pistachios

4. Press the mixture firmly into a lined baking tray.

5. Put the tray in the freezer for at least 1 hour to set.

6. Once set, cut into rectangular bars and dip each bar in melted dark chocolate, then sprinkle with a touch of sea salt and extra chopped pistachios.

7. Put the bars back in the freezer for 15 minutes to let the chocolate harden.

caption:
At 305 pounds, it was nearly impossible to imagine a world where I could actually be at a healthy body weight.

Let alone look like someone who’s fit.

It would require discipline I didn’t have, willpower I never had, and balance that was only ever theoretical in my head.

So even when I’d muster up the motivation to start a new weight loss plan, there was a part of me that had already prepared for my inevitable downfall.

Because I knew how I operated.

I had an “all-or-nothing” mindset.

At the time, I believed the only path to getting lean was finding balance, so I saw being all-or-nothing as a character flaw.

And it created a self-fulfilling prophecy:

Anytime I’d fall off track, I’d immediately point to my all-or-nothing tendencies as the culprit, and the idea of being “balanced” would feel increasingly distant.

But being all-or-nothing wasn’t the problem.

The problem was how I was choosing to relate to it.

The truth is, I had never considered the possibility that being all-or-nothing wasn’t something that I had to fix or get rid of.

Or that “balance” didn’t have to be the goal.

At least not at first.

So when I decided to embrace my all-or-nothing ways, that’s when things finally started clicking.

I still made plenty of mistakes.

But rather than letting them feed the previous narrative that I couldn’t be successful, I’d use them as data.

I learned what worked and what didn’t.

Most importantly, I learned what worked best for ME given the way MY brain worked.

And over time, this taught me that balance isn’t a destination.

It’s a feeling you gain from working WITH rather than against yourself.

So if you’re like me and have an all-or-nothing mindset, stop trying to change or fix it.

Your intensity isn’t the problem. It’s how you’re using and relating to it.

And to help you do this, I put together my Dieter Type Assessment, which will help you understand the way your brain works so you can make changes that turn your all-or-nothing mindset into a strength.

caption:
2026 marks 10 years since I started my online coaching business.

Over the last decade, I’ve seen countless diet and exercise trends come and go—most of which aren’t worth your time.

That’s not to say they’re harmful.

But they rarely deliver the results people expect.

That’s why I’m telling my clients to avoid these 4 trends in 2026.

~

#1 - Group Fitness Classes 

I get why people are attracted to these.

- You schedule and pay in advance. (accountability)
- You’re told exactly what to do. (simplicity)
- You can meet new people. (community)

For those reasons, I never tell my clients they CAN’T go.

But the truth is, your best results will come from following a workout plan designed specifically for YOUR goals and needs.

~

#2 - Worshipping Wearables 

I have an Oura ring to track my steps and sleep.

I enjoy looking at all the data it provides.

But they’re not the end all be all. 

Some of the data, particularly calories burned, is extremely inaccurate. 

And it’s easy to let the data dictate how you feel rather than listening to your body.

Wearables can be a tool, but they shouldn’t run your life.

~

#3 - Obsessing Over Seed Oils

It’s not my place to say whether or not you should be concerned about consuming seed oils. 

I’ll just say this: it’s a great example of majoring in the minors.

If your goal is to lose fat, build muscle, and improve your health, there are about 20 things that are much more important than worrying about whether seed oils are good or bad. 

~

#4 - Carnivore Diet 

It’s basically Keto, but with even more restrictions. 😅

A case can be made for people trying to fix autoimmune and gut health issues.

But even then, the benefits come from elimination rather than the diet itself.

For most people who just want to lose fat and improve their health, Carnivore is far from optimal.

For one, plant foods have fiber, nutrients, and tons of proven health benefits. They should absolutely be a part of your diet.

Plus, you basically have to make your entire life revolve around it for it to work, and most people don’t have the time, energy, discipline, or desire to do that.

~

Bottom Line: Stop chasing trends. Simplicity wins.

caption:

caption:
High protein, low effort. Under 15 minutes. I just can't be bothered cooking big meals these days.

Food tracking app: core by chloe ting

DINNER
Teriyaki chicken with broccolini for dinner
- 250g chicken thigh
- Avocado oil
- Teriyaki Sauce
- Ginger(optional)

Marinate chicken with teriyaki sauce if you want to.. it will be tastier but not necessary. You can always marinate it the night before and fry it the next day. 
Fry it on the pan until its deep brown and caramelized, turn the chicken and fry until deep brown on the other side too

Broccolini is cooked with avocado oil, garlic, lemon and oyster sauce. I use quite a lot of oil cause i like it oily, but if you're watching calories, you can just steam your vegetables! Broccoli is quite nice with just some salt too :)

SNACK
Protein chia seeds
- A bottle of chobani yogurt drink
- 2 tablespoons of chia seeds
- Berries

Mix the ingredients and let it set for 4 hrs or overnight. Topped it with your favorite fruits.

Stimulus and Strategy:⁣
Today’s workout is a monostructural grind with alternating run and row intervals — 3,000 meters of running and 3,000 meters of rowing total. The run distances descend while the row distances ascend. Pace this conservatively early on. The opening 1,000-meter run and the closing 1,000-meter row should not be all-out efforts. Each run/row pairing should take about 5-6 minutes; if you can maintain that pace, you’ll finish in roughly 25-30 minutes. Transitions matter. On both the run and the row, focus on getting moving first, then build your pace as you settle in. Stay relaxed on the run — chest up, eyes forward, shoulders down. On the row, drive with the legs and avoid over-pulling with the arms.⁣

caption:
Cable Back Exercise Mistakes (FIX THIS!)

Lat Pulldown Mistake: Keeping your shoulders pinned down for the entire movement. This limits your range of motion and prevents you from getting a full stretch in your lats.

Fix: As the bar travels back up, let your shoulders rise slightly so your lats can stretch. Then, as you pull the bar down, depress your shoulders and drive your elbows down toward your sides.

Cable Row Mistake: Shrugging your shoulders as you pull the handle. This shifts more tension to your upper traps instead of keeping the focus on your lats and mid-back.

Fix: Keep your shoulders down as you row. Think about pulling your elbows back, not shrugging the weight up. Your shoulders should stay away from your ears throughout the pull.

caption:
“FACE PULLS”: SET YOUR DEFAULT POSTURE UPRIGHT, MAKE YOUR SHOULDERS AND NECK STABLE •

This week’s Huberman Lab podcast features Jeff Cavalier of  @athleanx — he’s a licensed physical therapist, strength and conditioning coach known for helping people reach their fitness goals, overcoming pain and injury with specific movements and getting tremendous longevity from their fitness training. 

We sat down and talked about “the little things that allow you to do the big important things for your entire life” on the podcast. 

Yes it’s true: You need to do the basics. Men and women should do basic compound movements of pressing and pulling and for their legs …and do so with progressive resistance. Every week. 

But the issue people tend to run into is pain or injuries or challenges with imbalanced mechanics. Doing certain little things for just a few minutes per week can be the difference between lifelong pain-free training, great posture (at default— without having to think about it!) better breathing, better mobility, and on and on.

One of the key movements that every man and woman should do a few times a week at least are “face pulls” which is where you pull a rope from slightly above high-level on a cable machine (or you could use bands if you don’t have access to a cable machine) starting from a position where your hands are almost touching directly in front of you (arms straight) to what sort of looks like a “double biceps flexed pose”, but with your thumbs pointed back and  bit out & away from your ears. That’s the correct “external rotation” you want, which is essential… you can learn more about on the podcast. 

All the texting and sitting that we do nowadays has most people defaulting to internal rotation, chin down and C shaped… not good (for many reasons!).

A video of how to do face pulls correctly as well as train your arms correctly are available at the “Huberman lab clips” channel on You Tube. There is a short excerpt of it here as well.

Thank you, Jeff for being such a tremendous coach in public educator helping people get and stay super fit. We appreciate you!

All relevant links at: hubermanlab.com

Thank you for your interest in science!

THE BENEFITS OF “SPLITTING YOUR (TRAINING) SPLIT” WHEN LIFE GETS EXTRA BUSY•

My guest on the Huberman Lab podcast out now is Jeff Cavaliere, MSPT, CSCS, of @athleanx — physical therapist and certified strength and conditioning specialist and one of the world’s leading public educators on resistance training to build muscle size and strength, avoiding and overcoming injuries, and improving your posture and movement patterns (biomechanics). 

We discuss often-overlooked muscles and exercises that support decades of pain-free training and long-term progress. Jeff explains the best and most efficient ways to strengthen glutes, rotator cuff, neck, and foot muscles and connective tissues, and how to resolve back, hip, and other pain. 

We also cover the essentials of cardio, fat loss, and nutrition and how to make excellent and ongoing progress despite real-life training constraints. 

This episode is crucial for men and women as young as their teens, 20s, and 30s, all the way up to their 70s, 80s (and beyond) to be strong, mobile, and pain-free.

Here we are talking about how to get your training done in especially busy times. In those times rather than miss work workouts it could be very beneficial to actually “split your split. 

I personally don’t like to train late at night, (Jeff has no issue with it, so it’s individual) but there’s no reason why you couldn’t do this in the morning. Obviously best to do your whole program along with life, but you have to pick your priorities, and sometimes they’re just isn’t time to do it at all.

The original is likely my most-watched video, so I wanted to update it with better visuals and better variations.

If you can't do a pushup, don't let it ruin your day!

Fitness is a journey, and we're all at different places.

Just find a pushup variation that you CAN do safely and competently, and work it until you're able to hit a goal of sets and reps!

Then you can move on to a harder variation.

Here's the progression:

Wall Pushups - 3 sets of 50
Incline Pushups - 3 sets of 40
Advanced Incline Pushups - 3 Sets of 35
Kneeling Pushups - 3 sets of 30
Alternating Pushups - Until you can do Full Pushups! 

That's it! Let me know if you have any questions and I'll be happy to address them!

The links at the end will give MUCH more information on this process.

caption:
Creamy Chipotle Chicken & Potatoes🍗🍟🧀

One of the most indulgent meal prep recipes, so creamy, rich in flavour and packed with protein. Using a sheet pan is a game changer for batch cooking🔥

Macros Per Serving (6 Total)

548 Calories | 51g Protein | 52g Carbs | 17g Fat

Ingredients (Makes 6 Servings)

Chipotle Chicken Marinade
- 1200g Raw Boneless Chicken Thighs, trim excess fat
- 2.5 Tsp Salt
- 3 Tsp Parsley
- 3 Tsp Garlic Powder
- 3 Tsp Smoked Paprika
- 2.5 Tsp Cumin
- 3 Tsp Onion Powder
- 100g Chipotle Paste
- 1 and 1/2 Limes, juiced
- 30g or 6 Tsp Olive Oil
Let this marinate overnight if possible, way more flavor!

Crispy Seasoned Potatoes
- 1300g Raw Yellow Potatoes, cubed
- 2.5 Tsp Garlic Powder
- 3 Tsp Italian Herbs
- 3 Tsp Smoked Paprika
- 2.5 Tsp Onion Powder
- Avocado Cooking Spray, heavy pass

Creamy Chipotle Sauce
- 20g Light Butter
- 150-200g Red Onion, finely chopped
- 1.5 Tsp Salt
- 2 Tsp Italian Herbs
- 60-80g Chipotle Paste (depends how spicy you want it)
- 400g Light Evaporated Milk
- 110g Light Cream Cheese
- Freshly Chopped Parsley, garnish

👨‍🍳 Cooking Instructions

1. Trim excess fat from chicken thighs. Add seasonings, chipotle paste, lime juice, and olive oil. Mix well and marinate.
2. Heat a large pan on low, add butter and chopped red onion. Cook for 5-7 mins until softened and lightly browned. Add seasonings and chipotle paste, mix, and cook for another 5 mins until caramelised.
3. Keep the heat low, add evaporated milk and cream cheese. Stir continuously until smooth, rich, and creamy.
4. Cube up potatoes, add seasoning and cooking spray, then mix well. Spread on a lined sheet pan and roast at 200C / 390F for 25 mins until golden and crispy. Season with salt, then fold into the sauce with fresh parsley until fully coated.
5. Spread marinated chicken on sheet pan, oven bake 25 mins 200C / 390F until golden and juicy. Cut into cubes, serve with creamy potatoes and ENJOY!

caption:
Caramelized Onion Chicken Pasta🍗🧅🧀

This is the best creamy pasta sauce I have ever made! Pure comfort, so indulgent, made using simple ingredients for a fraction of the calories. Elevate your meal prep for the week🤌🏽🔥

Macros Per Serving (6 Total)

638 Calories | 58g Protein | 52g Carbs | 21g Fat

Ingredients (Makes 6)

Garlic Herb Chicken
- 1200g Raw Boneless Chicken Thighs
- 2 Tsp Salt
- 4 Tsp Spicy Italian Seasoning (brand: Schwartz)
- 3 Tsp Parsley
- 4 Tsp Garlic Granules or Powder
- 4 Tsp Paprika
- 6 Tsp or 30g Olive Oil

Caramelized Onions
- 200g Red Onion, thinly sliced
- 200g White Onion, thinly sliced
- 100g Sundried Tomatoes, drained and chopped
- 1 Tsp Salt
- 3 Tsp Italian Seasoning
- 2 Tsp Paprika
- 1 Whole Garlic Bulb, sliced from the top
- 10 Seconds Spray Avocado Oil Spray

Creamy Pasta Sauce
- 400-450g Light Evaporated Milk or Regular Milk
- 120g Light Cream Cheese
- 90-100g Grated Parmesan
- 20-25g Dark Soy Sauce
- 1-2 Tbsp Fresh Parsley, finely chopped
- 350g Spaghetti or Linguine, dry weight

👨‍🍳Instructions

1. Slice chicken thighs into cubes. Add seasoning and olive oil, mix well then set aside.
2. Slice red and white onion, add to large oven dish with chopped drained sundried tomatoes, seasonings and avocado oil spray. Mix well, place whole garlic in centre then cover with foil.
3. Oven bake for 45 mins at 190C/380F checking halfway. They should be golden and caramelized.
4. Squeeze in garlic, mix well and while dish is still hot, add parsley, soy sauce, parmesan, milk and cream cheese.
5. Stir continuously until melted and creamy. You can place back in the oven on low temp to thicken the sauce slightly. Add cooked pasta and fold gently till rich and indulgent.
6. In a lined large sheet pan, spread chicken then oven bake for 18 mins at 200C/400F and broil for 5 extra mins until golden and crispy. Serve with caramelized onion pasta and ENJOY!

caption:
A lot of beginners make the mistake of going slow on purpose because they’re so focused on nailing the technique or “feeling it”. The advanced lifter knows that while good technique is important you still need to go “all in” effort wise to see growth. 

You have to find a balance of maintaining technique that suits your goal for the exercise and being able to push as hard as possible. Stable exercises with good bracing make this much easier but that’s a topic for another video. 

The max time you’ll need in the eccentric is around 3-4 seconds for just about any exercise. Even for muscles that do experience “extra” (passive) tension in that portion of the rom. Anything past that will very likely end up reducing the total growth stimulus of the set as you’ll end up with less concentric contractions where you’re recruiting way more muscle fibers controlled by high threshold motor units. 

Before someone mentions it there could be reason to add isometrics at the end of the concentric if a muscle has good leverage there like a glute bridge for example. That is different from purposefully slowing the concentric for more TUT or so you can “focus on form/sensation”

I’ve been called every name, I’ve been dragged online and I’ve faced so many rejections you wouldn’t even know about. Often left embarrassed but never defeated.

Sure I’ve f’ed up so many times but isn’t that the entire point of growing and learning. 

Be brave enough to not be liked by all, be delusional enough to dream big and if that makes other feel uncomfortable then just remember you’re doing spending right. 

Love ya 🤍

caption:
Today marks a monumental moment in my life, and I want to share it with you all.

I am incredibly proud to announce that I have secured the rights to all intellectual property for my nonprofit foundation @projectpowerbykc . I founded Project Power with the vision of making a meaningful impact on the lives of as many teenage girls as possible. I remember hating PE growing up and feeling uncomfortable in PE kits. SO WHY NOT CHANGE IT!

For the past two years, we’ve been dedicated to providing teenage girls in UK schools with proper activewear, including sports bras that nearly 40% of them don’t own one and often feel uncomfortable while trying to be active. This year, we aim to gift a big 30,000 units of activewear to those in need.

I also noticed that the physical education curriculum is often dull and outdated. With the collaboration of some amazing personal trainers, we have already empowered nearly 10,000 teenage girls to engage in fitness, and we aren’t stopping there! We’re also working on an online portal designed to keep girls active and inspired…there’s so much more to accomplish!

While I celebrate these achievements, I want to emphasise something critical…the importance of owning your work.

Throughout my journey, I’ve faced significant challenges in business. I’ve been taken advantage of by others, including co-founders who have claimed credit for the hard work I poured my heart and soul into. I’ve often stayed silent, worried about being labeled an “emotional female founder.” But how can I advocate for young girls if I’m not in control of my own projects?

So, here’s my message: never let anyone diminish your accomplishments or rob you of your ownership. Stand your ground and take pride in your work! 💅🏽

caption:
450 million years in the making. 🪨💪

Fresh off HYROX NYC, after a race I absolutely crushed, I wasn’t quite done yet.

We found a 32kg piece of Central Park bedrock and put it to work.

Press to windmill. Strict press. Thruster. Reverse lunge. Bent press. Pistol squat.

A circuit built around a rock that has existed for roughly 450 million years. Long before the city. Long before the park. Long before any of us.

The lesson is simple.

The tool doesn’t matter.

Give a dedicated person a kettlebell, a sandbag, a barbell, or a chunk of bedrock and they’ll find a way to train. They’ll find a way to challenge themselves. They’ll find a way to keep moving forward.

The race was over. The work wasn’t.

caption:
Strength training can support independence, confidence, resilience, and the ability to move through daily life with greater ease and capability.

This is where identity-based motivation can become incredibly powerful. Exercise feels more meaningful and sustainable when they support the roles and values that matter most to you. It can be valuable to ask yourself:

“What does being strong mean to me right now?”
“What role does movement play at this stage of my life?”

The answers to these questions will naturally evolve over time, and that’s okay. A meaningful fitness journey isn’t about fitting into a single mold.

For some, strength may look like chasing performance goals in the gym. In others, it may simply mean having the energy and physical capacity to show up for yourself and the people around you.

caption:
Aiming for a little personal best, hopefully on the journey to a strict muscle-up (maybe? pls?) 🤞🌈🦦 ⠀
⠀⠀
My limit was 12kg/26lbs of added weight 6 weeks ago, and I’ve been chipping away at it with a couple of my go-to tricks for building maximal strength (which work for other exercises too 😘): ⠀
⠀⠀
🪄 Overemphasise form: take your current personal best weight and emphasise impecccccable, slightly *exaggerated* technique. That means a full bodied range of motion, slowing it down a little (no swinging!) and adding a small pause at the top of the movement. Imagine the perfect/slightly exaggerated exercise demo. That’ll build your strength further even without a weight change, and reduce the step up to your goal weight which you’ll typically hit with imperfect form at first (until you master it ofc) ⠀
⠀⠀
🪄Go *even* heavier + just hold the weight, train the negatives or fail: a chunk of increasing maximal force is psychological and also training the nervous system. I like overshooting the goal weight a touch (I’d strap on 24kg/50lbs when working towards 20kg/45lbs) and just holding the starting position for 5-8 seconds or training the negative (the eccentric, “easy” half of the movement) or intentionally failing if it’s a safe exercise to fail (like pull ups). That’ll help change the psychology a little and make that goal weight feel like a baby weight 🐣 ⠀
⠀⠀
🪄 Structure the workout right: strength goals always go first in the workout (after a warmup) so I’m full of energy ⚡️⚡️ with 3 mins rest time minimum between sets. Each set is only 1-2 reps max 😇 ⠀
⠀⠀
🪄 Expect to get stuck: bumping your strength means eating enough, sleeping enough and resting those muscles enough, and even then it takes time. Sometimes the weights will fly up, other times you’ll be stuck on the same weight for weeks until you find the missing piece 🧩 If that’s how it’s going, you’re no different to anyone else ✨🤍

caption:
Greens may help athletes improve their performance and benefit people with high blood pressure and peripheral artery disease. Greens are win-win—rich in nitrates and a good source of potassium. The nitrates from green leafy vegetables are converted to nitric oxide in our body, and potassium increases nitric oxide release.

Nitric oxide from vegetable nitrates, from greens, for instance, not only improves oxygen efficiency, but also oxygen delivery by vasodilation of blood vessels—that is, by opening up our arteries so there’s more blood flow. We can improve our artery function within minutes of consuming greens.

Of all the food groups analyzed by a team of Harvard University researchers, greens were found to be associated with the strongest protection against major chronic diseases. Each additional daily serving may reduce our risk of both heart attacks and strokes up to about 20 percent.

Greens can be added to nearly any meal—in soups, salads, sandwiches, smoothies, and on. If eating more greens, such as kale or collards, is intimidating to you, just chop them up and cook them down.

Watch the videos "Oxygenating Blood with Nitrate-Rich Vegetables" at https://bit.ly/3joxk0V and “Lowering Our Sodium-to-Potassium Ratio to Reduce Stroke Risk” at https://bit.ly/2sR8mfP to learn more.

1-2 tbsp pumpkin seeds⁠

Mix together and serve.

caption:
Mushrooms have been shown to slow breast cancer growth in lab studies, but what about in real life? https://see.nf/49ozGJk ⁠
⁠
Population studies offer some insight. While foods like soy and green tea are linked to lower breast cancer risk, they don’t fully explain why rates are much lower in some parts of the world.⁠
⁠
When researchers looked at mushroom intake, they found something striking:⁠
Women who ate the equivalent of just half a mushroom per day had significantly lower odds of breast cancer. (That’s only about 15 shrooms a month!)⁠
⁠
What’s even more striking is that a nearly 90% reduction in breast cancer odds is associated with combining that mushroom intake with drinking about half a teabag’s worth of green tea a day.⁠
⁠
This shows that small, consistent dietary habits may be linked to meaningful differences in risk.⁠
⁠

caption:
After 6 months of doing a mini-bulk and gaining +6kg in total… I would like to see my ab lines a little more again for summer 💖 Here is how the last 4 weeks went HAHA 😂🫣 Doesn’t matter, it was not the right time 🫶🏼 

🐸 Comment „Froschi“ if you want to have that small „important 10s“ plan you can see in the end 📝

🇩🇪 Nachdem ich 6 Monate einen Mini-Bulk gemacht habe und jetzt auf einem „Höchstgewicht“ (bitte mit Augenzwinkern aufnehmen, ist natürlich nicht viel) von 54kg angekommen bin (+6kg / zumindest auf die letzten 9 Jahre gesehen), möchte ich für den Sommer meine Bauchmuskeln wieder ein kleeeein bisschen mehr sehen. Ich will nicht viel abnehmen, nur einen Tick. Denn ehrlich gesagt fühle ich mich richtig wohl, schön und stark mit mehr Fleisch auf den Rippen! 

Wer aufgepasst hat weiß, dass ich euch das mit dem Abnehmen schon vor 4 Wochen erzählt, aber offen gesagt 0,0 durchgezogen habe 😂😂😂 Ja ich weiß - die ach so disziplinierte Pamela hat es nicht geschafft auch nur 1 Gramm abzunehmen - man mag es kaum glauben 😂 aber offen gesagt, es war nicht der richtige Zeitpunkt. Ich war so viel auf Reisen, war gestresst, hatte gar keine Routine, habe meine China Tour gemeistert und ihr könnt es euch denken - das zährt an einem. Deswegen wollte ich meinen Körper nicht noch weiter mit einem Kaloriendefizit stressen. Denn gesund bleiben und mit genügend Energie alle Aufgaben zu absolvieren - das war dann plötzlich doch mein Hauptfokus. Also, nochmal Start von neuem, ab jetzt dann eben. Passend dazu werde ich 6 Wochen 30 Jahre alt 🎂🎈

Seed oils, saturated fat, and the tradeoff people miss | Layne Norton, Ph.D.

-The core arguments against seed oils: the four main claims underlying the idea that seed oils are uniquely harmful, and how well they hold up once major confounders are addressed
-The historical trials that shaped the debate: the Minnesota Coronary Experiment, Sydney Diet Heart Study, Rose Corn Oil trial, and later studies replacing saturated fat with polyunsaturated fat
-Mechanisms and causality: LDL cholesterol, oxidized LDL, linoleic acid (omega-6), inflammation, -Mendelian randomization, and why lifetime LDL exposure matters more than per-particle oxidation risk
-Practical takeaways: industrial processing concerns, cooking oils, real-world dietary fat choices, and how to prioritize nutrition relative to calories, activity, and overall lifestyle factors

caption:
It’s been 1 week and 1 day since I last nursed Zane 🫶🏻

Breastfeeding was probably one of the hardest things the two of us had to learn together…

There were moments at 4 a.m. draining my boob over a sink before an event because of a clogged duct that I will never forget 🙈😩

And in the beginning… it felt SO hard.

But I’m so glad I kept going. I’m so grateful for every feed, every cuddle, and every moment. 

We had just transitioned him into his crib, and honestly I thought there was no way he’d ever sleep anywhere except right next to me. I truly couldn’t imagine it. But from the very first day in his crib, he slept through the night.

Last night he slept from 6:30 p.m. until 8 a.m. 😭

Even recently, putting him in a pack and play with a SlumberPod over the top… he just adapted so much quicker than I expected. It made me realize how capable these little humans really are. 🤷🏼‍♀️

So one day I just thought… let’s see if he’s ready.

We did our last feed, and over the next few days he barely asked. I’d distract him with water, a snack, a cuddle, and then suddenly… that chapter was over.

It’s emotional. Beautiful. Strange. Empowering. A little heartbreaking.

And if I’m honest… I’m also excited to have my boobs back 😂🤍

Oh and I got my cycle back just a week before I last nursed… maybe ready for the next round lol.

#breastfeedingjourney #postpartumfitnessjourney #postpartumbody

caption:
Most people butcher the dumbbell lateral raise and then wonder why their shoulders never grow.

The goal isn’t to see how much weight you can swing. The goal is to keep tension on the side delt from the first rep to the last. Start by slightly leaning your torso forward, keep a soft bend in the elbows, and think about driving your elbows out and away from your body rather than lifting the dumbbells up. Your hands are just along for the ride.

Another mistake I see all the time is people turning the movement into a full-body exercise. If your lower back is swinging, your knees are bouncing, or you’re using momentum to get the weight moving, you’ve already taken tension away from the muscle we’re trying to target. Slow the weight down, own every inch of the rep, and make the side delts do the work.

My favorite cue: lead with the elbows. Not the hands. Not the wrists. The elbows. When you focus on separating your elbows from your torso and reaching them outward, the side delts light up immediately and the movement becomes almost idiot-proof. Less ego. More tension. More growth.

caption:
Why Barbell & Free Weight Training Belongs In Your Program

Barbells and free weights are some of the most effective tools for building a complete physique. Unlike machines, they require your body to stabilize, balance, and coordinate movement while producing force. This not only recruits more muscle fibers, but also allows you to progressively overload key movements over time—one of the biggest drivers of muscle growth.

From a physique perspective, free-weight exercises like squats, presses, rows, lunges, and Romanian deadlifts help build the dense, thick, powerful look that most people are after. They develop foundational strength, improve athleticism, and create the muscle maturity that separates a good physique from a great one.

That doesn’t mean machines don’t have their place. The best programs utilize both. Free weights build the foundation, while machines and cables help isolate muscles, create targeted tension, and refine the details.

caption:
Despite the popular idea that a modest intake of alcohol is beneficial for our health, the research actually suggests there is no truly “safe” level of alcohol consumption when it comes to long-term health risk.

However, there’s a big difference between enjoying a leisurely glass of wine every now and then in the context of an otherwise healthy lifestyle… and throwing back multiple shots every day.

Health exists on a spectrum.

Let’s not pretend that alcohol is a health drink. At the same time, we don’t have to catastrophize the occasional glass of Cabernet Sauvignon. 🍷 

Ultimately, it’s up to you to make the best informed decision for yourself. 

In episode 20 of the All or Something Podcast, we discuss:

    ⁃    what the evidence says about alcohol and health
    ⁃    how alcohol impacts fat loss and muscle retention 

and more.

caption:
BMI (body mass index) is one of the most controversial tools in health and fitness. Some people say it’s outdated, inaccurate, and harmful. Others argue it’s still one of the most useful population health tools we have.

So… who’s right?

In this episode, we break down:
* where BMI came from
* what it was originally designed for
* what BMI actually measures
* whether BMI is useful for individuals
* why athletes and muscular people complicate the conversation
* how BMI relates to disease risk and mortality
* the biggest misconceptions about BMI
* weight stigma and the ethics of discussing body weight
* whether BMI should still be used in healthcare today

We also discuss how social media has shaped the BMI debate — and why many online conversations oversimplify both the science and the criticism.

This is not a “BMI is perfect” episode.
And it’s not a “BMI is meaningless” episode, either.

As usual, we aim for nuance over outrage.

caption:
“This doesn’t look healthy” is the definition of Stealth Health

*Calories and macro-nutrients are not the ONLY thing that matters - but they are the most important component of nutrition to master before focusing on niche elimination tactics*

The content I create is designed to help you master calorie control and focus on prioritizing protein intake and overall a balanced macro-nutrient profile, while enjoying the entire process. 

All recipes available on my page and in my cookbook! 

—

What I show breaks every convention we’ve been taught about weight loss… but if the conventions we’ve been taught in the past actually worked, you probably wouldn’t be watching this video

All the food I make intentionally looks very unhealthy, and as my name implies, that’s the whole point

When most of us begin a diet, or try to get “healthier”, the first step is to start cutting out all of the things we’ve labeled as “bad. People will tell you to follow a crazy range of elimination diets ranging from keto to whole 30. Some of these diets lead to short term success - but what you trade for that short term success is a long term dysfunctional relationship with food. If you listened to everyone’s advice on elimination diets - you’d very quickly realize virtually every food group is labeled as “bad” by some group of people. The secondary issue is that once you get to the 

Food is a constant - and a dysfunctional relationship with food leads to nothing but an excessively more difficult life.

My goal is to help you shift your thinking when starting a diet - instead of asking what in your diet is bad and must be removed… I want you to ask how can we take the things we’ve labeled as “bad” and turn them into something better

Restricting yourself from having food you love isn’t necessary. 

The less you feel like you’re dieting, the better.

My story + the journey to pitching a national retailer

caption:
🍦 This Protein Ice Cream Series has honestly changed my life.

I’ve been making macro friendly recipes for 12+ years and the perfect protein ice cream recipe has always evaded me.

Until the start of this series.

22 Protein Ice Cream Recipes.

All around 300-400 calories for a whole pint with 40g protein!

From Cosmic Brownie, Biscoff Cookie Butter, Fruity Pebble Cereal Milk, Cinnamon Toast Crunch Cereal Milk, Birthday Cake Batter…. the list goes on and on so it’s safe to say we’ll never run out of protein ice cream flavor options!

I hope you guys have enjoyed this series as much as I have 🤤

And because I want you guys to make protein ice cream on the daily….

I created a FREE Protein Ice Cream Recipe book with all 22 of these recipes 🍨

Links in my bio to snag your copy. Literally takes less than 15 seconds 🫡

Let’s get into my top Protein Ice Cream Tips:

1️⃣ Your Milks Matter

It’s a balance that allows for the lowest calorie count possible.

If you just use all almond milk, you risk a less creamy outcome just because of how much water content there is in almond milk.

You can by all means just use all Fairlife milk as well but it’ll just add an extra 40 ish calories.

2️⃣ Not All Protein Powders are made equal

They will be making up around 50% (sometimes 60%+) of the dry ingredients in pretty much all creami recipes IF you want the macros to be immaculate.

So a high quality whey/casein blend protein powder is a must.

One with an amazing flavor profile because it will be arguably the big contributor to flavoring of the pint.

And one that also does not have that chalky protein aftertaste because it will come through.

3️⃣ Meal Prep your pints.

I make 6 at a time with varying flavor so I have variety.

I use a small milk frother to mix the ingredients together. Works great!

4️⃣ Freezer pints with cover off.

This will ensure you don’t get the hump which has been known to break machines.

caption:
I’ll be honest with you…

I was never one of those women who loved exercise. I spent most of my life avoiding it, too busy raising kids, working, taking care of everyone else.

By the time I had a moment to breathe, I was 70, tired, and on more medications than I’d like to admit. I wasn’t looking for a transformation. I just wanted to feel like myself again.

So I started small. Embarrassingly small. But I started thanks to the nudges of my daughter @michellemacdonaldofficial and something funny happened…the more I moved, the more I could move. 

Slowly, things shifted. My energy came back. I got off most of those medications. And I started actually enjoying my life again.

I’m 80 now and I move better than I did ten years ago.
I’m not telling you this to impress you. I’m telling you because I was exactly where you are…tired, skeptical, wondering if it was too late.

It wasn’t…and it’s not too late for you either.

caption:
At 70 years old, I was tired. My health was failing, my joints ached, and honestly, I felt completely overwhelmed by how far I had let myself go. 

When I first looked at the gym, I was intimidated. I felt like I didn’t belong there, and a big part of me just wanted to stay comfortable, even if that “comfortable” meant being sick.

But I knew I needed a change. So, despite the fear and the exhaustion, I didn’t let it stop me.

I took that very first step, and then I took another. I kept going, and I kept pushing…even on the days when progress felt painfully slow. 

Day by day, meal by meal, workout by workout, I built a brand-new life. I didn’t just get healthier; I became the absolute best, most vibrant version of myself.

If a 70-year-old grandmother can completely transform her life, I promise you that you can too. You are never too old, and it is never too late to choose yourself.
